args.body:
Hi Dora! I just had a look at your personal website (www.dora-website.com) and wanted to share some feedback.

What I liked:
- It's clean and loads instantly — no clutter, no pop-ups, no autoplay video. That's a genuinely good foundation.
- The page tells the reader right away what it's about and how to reach you, which is exactly what a personal site should do.

Where I'd suggest some improvement:
- The site is currently just one line of text, so there's not much for a visitor to actually engage with. Even a short "About Me" section with a photo, a couple of sentences about your work/interests, and links to your projects or socials would make it feel much more like a real home on the web.
- Consider adding a small portfolio or blog section — even three or four short entries would give people a reason to come back.
- A bit of visual personality would help too: some color, a simple layout, or a header image. Right now it reads more like a placeholder than a finished site.
- If you do list contact details, you may want to add a contact form as well, so people don't have to open their email client.

Overall, a nice, no-nonsense starting point — it just needs a bit more content and personality to really show who you are. Happy to share more specific thoughts if you're interested!

Best,
Emma Johnson
Blue Sparrow Tech

Hi Eve! I visited your blog (www.eve-blog.com) and wanted to send you some feedback.

What I liked:
- The site is refreshingly simple and fast — no heavy scripts, no distracting pop-ups, and the message is clear right away.
- Hiking is a fantastic subject for a blog. It's visual, active, and there's always something new to write about, so you have great raw material to work with.

Where I'd suggest some improvement:
- Right now the blog is a single line of text, so there's no actual reading experience yet. Publishing a few real posts would be the biggest win — even short photo-heavy write-ups about local trails would give visitors a reason to subscribe.
- Since hiking is your thing, photos and maps would be your strongest asset. A gallery or trail map per post would make the blog much more engaging than text alone.
- Adding an "About" section, plus a way for readers to subscribe (RSS, email, or a newsletter) would help turn casual visitors into regulars.
- A little structure would help too — categories or tags for things like "Day Hikes," "Gear," or "Trip Reports" make a blog much easier to navigate as it grows.
- Some visual warmth in the design (earth tones, trail-inspired imagery) would reinforce the theme nicely.

Overall, a great concept and a clean foundation — it just needs some actual posts and a bit of structure to bring it to life. I'd love to read more once you start publishing!

Best,
Emma Johnson
Blue Sparrow Tech
